Kerosene180 to 26010 to 16Jet aircraft fuel
Diesel260 to 32016 to 20Fuel for buses and lorries
Fuel oil320 to 40020 to 50Industrial heating
Bitumen400 to 600More than 50Surfacing roads

mcqs.q: What is petroleum?
options: A natural substance trapped in rocks beneath the earth's crust
A man-made fuel produced in factories
A gas found above the earth's crust
mcqs.why: Petroleum is a natural substance trapped in rocks beneath the earth's crust; its name means rock oil. It is not a single pure hydrocarbon but a complex combination of gaseous, liquid and solid hydrocarbons.

mcqs.q: Petroleum is a complex combination of:
options: Gaseous, liquid and solid hydrocarbons, with water, salts and earth particles also present
mcqs.why: Petroleum is a complex combination of gaseous, liquid and solid hydrocarbons, in which water, salts and earth particles are also present. It is a liquid lighter than water and does not dissolve in it.

mcqs.q: Which statement about petroleum is correct?
options: It is heavier than water and dissolves in it
It is a liquid lighter than water and does not dissolve in it
It is a solid heavier than water
mcqs.why: The notes state that petroleum is a liquid lighter than water and does not dissolve in it. This is why it floats on water rather than mixing with or sinking in it.

mcqs.q: Why is petroleum called 'Black Gold'?
options: Because it is found only in gold mines
Because it is black and worthless
Because it is black and as valuable as gold
mcqs.why: Petroleum is called Black Gold because it is black and as valuable as gold. From it petrol, diesel, kerosene, gas, plastics and many other things are obtained, and it is the main source of the economy and energy of countries.

mcqs.q: How is petroleum separated into fractions?
options: By fractional distillation in refineries in fractionating columns
mcqs.why: Petroleum is separated into fractions by fractional distillation, which is done in refineries in fractionating columns. The column is cold at the top and hot at the bottom, so fractions are collected according to their boiling ranges.

mcqs.q: In a fractionating column, the temperature is:
options: Cold at the top and hot at the bottom
Hot at the top and cold at the bottom
mcqs.why: The fractionating column is cold at the top and hot at the bottom. Because of this temperature gradient, fractions with low boiling ranges rise to the top while heavier fractions stay lower down.

mcqs.q: Which fraction has a boiling range of 40 to 110 °C and is used as car fuel?
mcqs.why: Petrol has a boiling range of 40 to 110 °C, contains 5 to 8 carbons, and is used as car fuel. Naphtha boils higher, from 110 to 180 °C, and is used for plastics.

mcqs.q: Naphtha, with 8 to 10 carbons, is used for:
mcqs.why: Naphtha has a boiling range of 110 to 180 °C and 8 to 10 carbons, and it is used for plastics. Jet aircraft fuel is kerosene, and surfacing roads is the use of bitumen.

mcqs.q: Which fraction is used as jet aircraft fuel?
mcqs.why: Kerosene, with a boiling range of 180 to 260 °C and 10 to 16 carbons, is used as jet aircraft fuel. Petrol is car fuel and diesel is fuel for buses and lorries.

mcqs.q: Bitumen contains more than 50 carbons and is used for:
mcqs.why: Bitumen has the highest boiling range, 400 to 600 °C, with more than 50 carbons, and is used for surfacing roads. Industrial heating is the use of fuel oil, which has 20 to 50 carbons.

lessons.title: Pharmaceutical Industry
lessons.notes_html:
What is the Pharmaceutical Industry?

The pharmaceutical industry researches, manufactures, sells and distributes drugs for the prevention, treatment and cure of illnesses.

Importance

  • Treatments increase life expectancy.
  • The objective to eradicate diseases is achieved, for example the elimination of smallpox.
  • Pain and suffering are reduced.
  • Vaccines save money, because prevention is cheaper than treatment.
  • Hospital stays are shorter.
  • The industry employs millions of people.
  • Pharmaceutical companies boost the global economy.

mcqs.q: What does the pharmaceutical industry do?
options: It researches, manufactures, sells and distributes drugs
It only sells medicines in pharmacies
It only treats patients in hospitals
mcqs.why: The pharmaceutical industry researches, manufactures, sells and distributes drugs. Its work covers the whole chain from research to distribution, not just selling or treating patients.

mcqs.q: Drugs are produced by the pharmaceutical industry for:
options: The prevention, treatment and cure of illnesses
mcqs.why: The industry produces drugs for the prevention, treatment and cure of illnesses. Prevention and treatment are just as much its purposes as cure, so options naming only one purpose are incomplete.

mcqs.q: How do treatments from the pharmaceutical industry affect life expectancy?
options: They have no effect on life expectancy
mcqs.why: The notes list as an importance of the industry that treatments increase life expectancy. Effective medicines help people live longer, which is one of its major benefits to society.

mcqs.q: Which disease is given as an example of the objective to eradicate diseases being achieved?
mcqs.why: The elimination of smallpox is given as the example of the objective to eradicate diseases being achieved. No other disease is named in the notes as an example of eradication.

mcqs.q: How does the pharmaceutical industry help patients regarding pain?
options: Pain is ignored by the industry
Pain is treated only by surgery
mcqs.why: One importance of the pharmaceutical industry is that pain and suffering are reduced through its drugs. Relieving suffering is a direct benefit of the medicines it researches and manufactures.

mcqs.q: Why do vaccines save money?
options: Because prevention is cheaper than treatment
Because hospitals charge less for vaccines
mcqs.why: Vaccines save money because prevention is cheaper than treatment. Preventing an illness with a vaccine costs less than treating the illness after it occurs.

mcqs.q: What happens to hospital stays because of the pharmaceutical industry?
mcqs.why: The notes state that hospital stays are shorter as a result of the pharmaceutical industry's drugs. Effective treatments help patients recover faster and leave hospital sooner.

mcqs.q: What does the pharmaceutical industry provide in terms of employment?
options: It employs only a few scientists
mcqs.why: The pharmaceutical industry employs millions of people. This large-scale employment is listed among its importances, alongside its contribution to health and the economy.

mcqs.q: What is the pharmaceutical industry's effect on the global economy?
options: Pharmaceutical companies boost the global economy
It works only in one country
mcqs.why: Pharmaceutical companies boost the global economy, as stated in the notes. Together with employing millions of people, this makes the industry economically important as well as medically important.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT listed as an importance of the pharmaceutical industry?
options: Medicines become more expensive for everyone
mcqs.why: The notes list increased life expectancy, reduced pain and suffering, vaccines saving money, shorter hospital stays, employment for millions and a boost to the global economy as importances. Making medicines more expensive for everyone is not listed as an importance.
